subject: Private VPC deployment — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmehealth.com>, Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC deployment — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Emily & Rajiv — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and the agreed next steps.

Top pain points you shared:
- Regulatory/data residency: all patient data must remain in Acme Health-managed GCP projects in us-east-1; logs retained per HIPAA/Soc2 controls.
- Network constraints: strict egress rules, no public outbound IPs allowed; allowlist only to specific Redwood control-plane endpoints and a fixed set of artifact URLs.
- Air-gap/segmented environments: some environments will be air-gapped; need an offline install option for inference workloads and periodic sync to the control plane via a bastion/approved egress path.
- Auditability: detailed audit logs and KMS/HSM integration required for keys and access.

Goals we captured:
1) Proof-of-concept private deployment in your dev VPC (non-production) in 6-8 weeks.
2) Network runbook and connectivity checklist completed prior to infra run.
3) Evaluate performance/latency with a subset of models and production-like data.

Immediate next steps (ownership):
- Camila: share network diagram and connectivity checklist (attached) + proposed date options for infra/security sync.
- Marissa: provide SCA questionnaire answers and ops playbook for offline/private installs (attached).
- Lukas: lead technical deep-dive on the VPC peering/egress pattern and quantization/perf tradeoffs in the POC.
- Emily/Rajiv: confirm the internal security and procurement participants and your preferred dates for the infra call.

Attachments: acme_health_network_diagram.pdf (network boundaries + NAT/bastion callouts), acme_health_sca_questionnaire_filled.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-deploy-playbook.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with 3 time slots for the infra/security sync and a short checklist to unblock procurement.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our notes and priorities. A couple clarifications:
- For the air-gapped sites, we will need a one-way controlled egress to pull model artifacts; no outbound SSH allowed. We can share the approved artifact S3/GCS endpoints.
- Our legal team will want a high-level data flow diagram for the PoC (happy this was included).

Attendees to add for the infra/security call: Rajiv (CTO) and our Head of Security, Maya Patel (maya.patel@acmehealth.com). Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) is looped for timeline/POC contracting — they prefer a short MSA + SOW for POC.

Proposed windows next week (all ET):
- Tue 6/8 between 10-12
- Wed 6/9 between 2-4
Please let us know what works.

Best,

Looping in a couple quick notes from the solutions/ops side:
- Attached is the completed SCA questionnaire (acme_health_sca_questionnaire_filled.pdf) — covers our encryption, key management, and isolation controls.
- For the air-gapped option, our offline installer requires a small checklist: approved bastion IP, outbound allowlist for artifact downloads (we can sign the artifacts and provide checksums), and a short maintenance window for periodic syncs. I put the full checklist in the playbook PDF attached.
- Lukas — can you confirm the expected NAT/egress patterns we should ask Acme to provision? I recommend we request both: (1) a private peering for low-latency traffic between their GPU subnet and our managed infra (if allowed), OR (2) a small NAT with strict allowlist to our artifact endpoints + control plane for telemetry only.

HubSpot deal: RDW-ACME-2027-05 (I've added notes and the SCA to the record).
